summary: The LLM landscape in 2026 is dominated by a handful of frontier families from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, with strong open-weight competition from Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral, and Alibaba's Qwen. Real-world enterprise adoption is increasingly driven by aggregator availability (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx), which amplifies the reach of models well beyond their direct-API usage. The research data contains several speculative or unreleased model names (e.g. GPT-6, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4), which have been omitted in favor of confirmed, currently available models.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: Consistently the highest-volume model across developer surveys and API usage, and available through Azure OpenAI and multiple aggregators, giving it the broadest enterprise reach.
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications requiring text, vision, and audio.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Confirmed in research as shipped Feb 17 matching Opus-level performance at Sonnet pricing; widely adopted for coding and available via AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex.
models.best_for: Enterprise coding assistants and agentic workflows.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Noted in research as the 'Context Window King' with massive adoption through Google Vertex AI and tight Google Cloud/Workspace integration.
models.best_for: Large-document analysis and multimodal enterprise workloads.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: High-volume low-cost workhorse with a large context window, broadly consumed through Vertex AI for cost-sensitive production workloads.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Confirmed current Anthropic model; popular for high-volume, low-latency tasks and available across AWS Bedrock and Vertex AI aggregators.
models.best_for: High-volume lightweight tasks and real-time assistants.

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: Research describes it as the cheapest frontier-class reasoning model ($0.55/$2.19 per 1M tokens) with huge open-weight HuggingFace download volume and availability on Bedrock and Azure.
models.best_for: Reasoning-heavy and algorithmic tasks on a budget.

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: Widely downloaded open-weight MoE model offering near-frontier performance at a fraction of the cost; broadly self-hosted and available via aggregators.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: One of the most downloaded open-weight models on HuggingFace and widely available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx for enterprise self-hosting.

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Leading European frontier model available through Azure, AWS Bedrock, and Vertex AI, favored for data-residency-sensitive enterprise deployments.
models.best_for: European enterprise deployments needing data sovereignty.

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: Top-ranked open-weight model family on HuggingFace with rapidly growing global downloads and strong multilingual/coding performance.

models.name: o3
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI's dedicated reasoning model with strong adoption for complex problem-solving, available via the OpenAI API and Azure OpenAI, clustering closely with the top open-weight models in usage.
models.best_for: Complex reasoning, research, and analytical tasks.
